query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled rapid thermal annealing (RTA) treatment that refines the microstructure and induces a modest phase subdivision in an equiatomic, five‐component FeCoNi‐based high-entropy alloy will increase domain wall pinning and thereby raise the coercivity relative to the soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
generation.material_initial_state: An equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy (with two additional elements chosen to fulfill the multicomponent and >1.0R entropy criteria) that crystallizes as a single-phase FCC solid solution with low intrinsic coercivity and high saturation magnetization.
generation.intervention: Apply a rapid thermal annealing (RTA) step with an optimized time‐temperature profile (e.g., annealing at ~600°C–700°C for a short duration) under an inert atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Inert atmosphere; temperature around 600–700°C; short annealing duration to avoid complete homogenization yet induce grain refinement and strain; relevant to processing bulk or thin film specimens.
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain structure with enhanced density of grain boundaries and minor, coherent secondary phase/nano-precipitates that create strain and local anisotropy.
generation.mechanism: The RTA treatment increases coercivity by reducing grain size and introducing microstructural defects and strain fields that act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls, thus requiring a higher external field to reverse magnetization.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in the coercivity (Hc) compared to the baseline soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys, while potentially causing a modest reduction in saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: Previously reported equiatomic FeCoNi-based HEAs alloyed with Pd or Pt that exhibit low coercivity due to their high-symmetry single-phase FCC structure.
generation.boundary: This enhancement in coercivity is expected only if the RTA parameters are finely tuned; excessive annealing may lead to complete homogenization or unwanted phase transformations that negate the pinning effect.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and may depend sensitively on the annealing profile and the precise microstructural evolution; experimental optimization is necessary.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize the equiatomic, five-component FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy and divide the sample into two groups. Subject one group to the optimized RTA treatment (600–700°C for the prescribed short duration in an inert atmosphere) while keeping the other group as a control (either as-cast or conventionally annealed at high temperature without rapid cycling). Measure and compare the magnetic hysteresis loops, focusing on coercivity (Hc) values.
measurements: Hysteresis loop using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM)
Grain size and microstrain characterization via XRD and electron microscopy
Phase distribution using TEM or SEM-EDX analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RTA-treated alloy does not show a statistically significant increase in coercivity (Hc) relative to the control sample (i.e., if Hc remains comparable to or lower than that measured for the FeCoNiPd/Pt derivatives), the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Therefore, the bimodal coercivity distribution observed in the OOP direction is explained by a 2‐step process of magnetization reversal beginning with easy domain nucleation and propagation in the large (001) oriented grains (narrow low Hc peak), followed by pinning between grains with small size and varying easy‐axis direction (broad high Hc peak). The distribution of size and easy‐axis orientation both manifest in the spreading of the high Hc peak along the Hc axis. Based on this, we expect that the Hc could be enhanced through microstructural optimization such as a reduction in grain size, which may be achieved by adjusting the RTA time and temperature.

In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

cited_evidence.kind: web:Dislocation mechanisms for fcc to hcp phase transformation
cited_evidence.text: We have shown the existence of a nanostructure with hcp phase in the equiatomic CrCoNi—an alloy widely considered to have a single-phase fcc structure. We observed a delineation between CrCoNi—with hcp as the ground state independent of the local atomic arrangements—and the CrCoMnFeNi HEA, where the magnetic frustration resulting from the addition of Mn breaks a clear trend for relative hcp vs fcc energies. In addition, we showed that there is no driving force for this phase transformation in any other equiatomic ternary derivatives of this HEA. These findings emphasize the fact that high-entropy alloys with more constituent elements are not necessarily superior to their derivatives. Instead, the combination of chemical and, as emphasized presently, magnetic identities of elements govern the properties. An important consequence of this finding is that new alloying combinations can be predicted based on similar favorable magnetic properties. These results provide a new paradigm for design of single-phase alloys with metastable structures through computational guidance and experimental validation.
